text:
maria: heads up — proposing a new GPU nodepool in eastus2 to support low-cost inference traffic. thinking L4-backed nodes for most realtime shading + a small ND96 (A100-ish) pool for heavy tails. cost delta looks promising.
ajay: can you paste the sizing/cost numbers? also any quota constraints in eastus2? last time we hit a regional quota for ND series.
maria: rough numbers: L4-equivalent SKU (inference) ~ $0.80/hr, ND96asr_v4 (A100 v4) ~ $4.10/hr. target initial size = 4 L4 nodes + 2 ND96 nodes (gpu-per-node 8/8). will autoscale based on app labels.
kevin: are we using spot/preemptible for L4? that's the main levers for cost.
maria: yes prefer spot for L4 pool, with fallback to on-demand ND pool when spot capacity is low. plan: create 2 nodepools — gpu-infer-spot (spot, tainted: gpu=infer:NoSchedule) and gpu-heavy (on-demand, tainted: gpu=heavy:NoSchedule).
sofia: note: cluster-autoscaler annotations? scale-down grace for GPU nodes needs to be tuned otherwise we thrash with bursty traffic.
ajay: +1. We should set cluster-autoscaler max-unready=10 and scale-down-delay-after-add=10m for gpu pools. also use balance-similar-node-groups=false because we mix SKUs.
kevin: are we handling GPU device plugin metrics? scale decisions must account for GPU-allocatable resources reported by kubelet.
maria: yep — device-plugin v1.11 deployed on the cluster. also enabling Alpha feature 'node.kubernetes.io/accelerator' label in our taint/selector combos.
oncall-bot: [alert] region eastus2 quota remaining for ND96asr_v4: 3/10. Submit quota increase request to avoid provisioning failures.
maria: opened Azure support ticket 789321 and requested +10 ND96 per subscription. ETA ~48-72h. ticket link: https://portal.azure.com/#support/tickets/789321
sofia: small ops concern — draining GPU nodes with attached local ephemeral state can cause pod eviction failures. we should annotate workloads with pod-disruption-budget and graceful termination to help scale-down.
maria: agreed. plan to add this to the rollout checklist. sample toleration/taint YAML we will use:
```
# nodepool taint
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=gpu-infer-spot gpu=infer:NoSchedule

# pod toleration snippet
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "infer"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
ajay: for creation, terraform snippet looks like:
```
resource "azurerm_kubernetes_cluster_node_pool" "gpu_infer_spot" {
  name                = "gpu-infer-spot"
  kubernetes_cluster_id = azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.rw_cluster.id
  vm_size             = "Standard_NC6as_T4_v3" # example L4-like
  enable_auto_scaling = true
  min_count           = 0
  max_count           = 10
  orchestrator_version = "1.28.2"
  spot_max_price      = -1
  tags = { pool = "gpu-infer" }
}
```
kevin: confirm node image + drivers: we need NVIDIA driver 535+ and CUDA runtime pinned for ND96. Also validate GPU plugin DaemonSet tolerations so they schedule on spot nodes.
maria: driver install will be baked into the node image via custom VHD. infra-runbook updated. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/gpu-node-images
sofia: testing plan?
maria: smoke test: 1) create pool with 1 node, 2) deploy small inference service that requests 0.5 GPUs, 3) send traffic to verify autoscale up/down, 4) simulate spot eviction to ensure workload drains and falls back to ND pool. will run in staging first.
kevin: what about networking egress — eastus2 has some bandwidth caps on ND96; we should avoid colocating heavy training jobs in that pool.
ajay: agree. tag pools with cost-center and include egress monitoring. set quota alert if average egress > 2Gbps over 5m window.
maria: requesting approval to provision staging pools now (small sizes). cost estimate for staging for 7 days ~ $180.
sofia: approve for staging. prod waits until ticket resolves and quota confirmed.
maria: thanks. I'll kick off terraform apply for staging and update this thread with ticket and smoke results.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: terraform plan for gpu-infer-spot (staging) — run_id=plan-20260623-01
maria: noted. I'll watch. :eyes:
